title: Review Module
description: The opening module that reloads the whole of second year before the new programme begins: reporting somebody's words (say against tell, the that-clause, the shift of pronouns and possessives, the backshift of tenses and of will into would, here into there); let and make followed by an object and the base verb, and the to that comes back in was made to; used to for a finished past habit against be used to for a present one; the four ways of comparing (-er/more than, the -est/the most, as ... as, not ... enough) and the double comparative the more ... the -er; the present perfect against the simple past, with since, for and the present perfect continuous of a period that reaches today; the passive of simple tenses, of modals (can be used) and of verbs with two objects (the winners were given); the linkers of cause, result, contrast and addition; what holds a text together — chronological order, reference words and a deleted part put back where it belongs; the five blocks of a business letter; and word building, from a verb or an adjective to the noun, the adjective and the adverb English builds on it, including the words stacked in front of a noun in a lung-testing machine
